roof_age_underwriting.text: Carriers increasingly treat roof age and condition as a primary factor in insurability, pricing and terms. Common structure: roofs ~0-10 years old at replacement cost; 10+ years moved to a roof payment schedule (prorated by age); ~15+ years may be actual cash value (ACV) only for wind/hail. Maryland brokers note older buildings sometimes need roof (and electrical/plumbing) updates before a carrier will quote. Most published roof-schedule material describes personal lines; commercial roof schedules and ACV roof endorsements exist but thresholds are carrier-specific, so there is no Maryland-published standard. For PaxSeal: documented inspections and repair records are the evidence an underwriter asks for when a roof is past 10 years.

roof_life_years.climate_note: IECC climate zone 4A (mixed-humid). Roofs see hot humid summers (NRI heat wave Relatively High in PG/AA, Very High in Baltimore Co.), frequent summer thunderstorm wind (NRI ~7-8 strong-wind event-days/yr per county) and winter freeze-thaw with snow/ice (winter weather Relatively High in all five counties; ice storm Moderate-High). Freeze-thaw drives seam/flashing fatigue and ice-dam/ponding damage at drains; heat/UV drives membrane aging. No source was found that quantifies a Maryland-specific roof-life adjustment, so none is applied.

code_triggers.text: (1) Code basis: Maryland Building Performance Standards (COMAR 09.12.51) require every jurisdiction to enforce the same I-code editions; the 2021 IBC/IRC/IECC/IEBC were adopted statewide effective May 29 2023, with local enforcement required by May 29 2024. Maryland published proposed 2024 I-code adoption in the Maryland Register on June 26 2026 (comments closed July 27 2026), so a 2024-code cycle is imminent. Howard County has already adopted the 2024 suite locally. (2) Recover limits (IBC 1511.3.1.1): a roof recover is NOT permitted where the existing roof/covering is water-soaked or deteriorated to the point it is not an adequate base, or where the existing roof already has two or more applications of any covering; in those cases a full tear-off is required. This is the direct link between neglect and cost: trapped moisture from unrepaired leaks turns a recover/restoration option into a full tear-off. (3) Energy code on re-roof (IECC C503.3.1, 2021): roof replacement on a roof with insulation entirely above deck must meet the prescriptive insulation (C402.1.3/.4/.5 or C407) for the climate zone (4A here); total R-value may not be reduced; minimum 1 in. at drains/scuppers. A Baltimore cost source cites R-25 to R-35 polyiso at $2.00-3.50/sq ft, a large add-on to a tear-off. (4) Damage thresholds: no Maryland- or county-specific percentage-of-damage rule forcing full replacement (like Florida's 25% rule) was found; IEBC repair provisions apply.
